titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 2/2006 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ސެކިއުރިޓީޒް ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Securities Act (Law no. 2/2006) so that it links to the Business Registration Act (Law no. 18/2014). It rewrites parts of Article 10 and Article 41, adds a new Article 41-1 and adds a new item to a list in Article 63. The new text of Article 10 and the new Article 41-1 both name the Business Registration Act. It would take effect three months after it is ratified and published. The scans are hard to read, so the exact rules are uncertain.
whyItMatters: It changes how the securities law and the business-registration law fit together, which could affect businesses that deal in securities. The scans are too hard to read to say exactly how.
keyProvisions: Article 1 replaces several sub-paragraphs of Article 10 and sets out a new text. A new paragraph cites the Business Registration Act (18/2014) by name, and its exact rule is hard to read.

Article 2 adds a new Article 41-1 after Article 41. It has a numbered list of three points (1) to (3) and further paragraphs that refer back to the Business Registration Act. The detail is hard to read.
Article 3 adds a new item (14) after item (13) in Article 63. The wording of the new item could not be read reliably.
Article 4 says the amendment takes effect three months after it is ratified and published.
whoIsAffected: Businesses that are registered under the Business Registration Act and deal in securities, though the scans do not name them clearly.
statedReasons: An explanatory note is printed and refers to the Business Registration Act (18/2014) and the Securities Act (2/2006). It is too hard to read to state its reasons reliably.
